items.note: Three thick curved arrows closing a ring around a solid centre disk lettered 'Sustainable development', with the three sector labels set outside the ring: Social at the left, Environment at the upper right, Economic at the foot. The disk carries a faint checkered fill and the arrows a dotted fill, so the three aspects are distinguished by position only. No axis, no scale, no number, no legend box - the labels are drawn straight onto the picture. note:
Paper 86, Team 35780. Twenty-one measured regions over fourteen of the twenty-four pages, all
twenty-one accounted for: fourteen figure rows, six table rows, one exclusion, so unaccounted is
zero and nothing is left unresolved. The paper numbers fourteen figures and seven tables, and this
record carries all of them except Table 2, which is printed on p9 as a plain text grid with no rules
at all and therefore owns no measured region - it is a declared gap, not a guess.

The region pass had one easy case and one awkward one. The easy case is the summary sheet: the p1
region is a single 0.77-area vector cluster because the T1-T4 and F1-F4 fill-in rules and the
sheet's separator line span the page, which is page furniture and not an exhibit, so it is excluded.
The awkward case is that this paper draws eight of its fourteen figures as two-column pairs -
Figures 3 and 4 on p12, 5 and 6 on p13, 7 to 10 on p17, 11 and 12 on p18 - and each pair is pasted
as separate bitmaps, so every half is its own region and its own row, with its own printed caption.
That is also why the text layer reads like a puzzle: it interleaves the two captions of a pair into
one run, "Figure 3: Forecast on comprehensive Figure 4: The GE-Matrix for sustainability of
performances of three countries three countries", so all eight of those captions are typed from the
crops and marked as such.

What the pictures actually show, read off the crops one at a time. Figure 1 is a three-arrow ring
labelled Social, Environment and Economic around a centre disk, with no arrowhead on the left arc, so
its cycle direction is only half stated. Figure 2 is the GE-Matrix as nine shaded blocks over a
ten-by-ten lattice, numbered I to IX from the bottom left, with four fill classes and no key - and
the numerals sit half a cell off the blocks they name, so the picture encodes the same nine regions
twice and the two encodings disagree. Figures 3 and 4 are the two-column pair on p12: nine forecast
curves whose Congo half collapses into an unreadable knot near 0.05, and three two-point trajectories
in the CI/DI plane with no time axis. Figures 5 and 6 are the same control loop drawn twice, before
and after the plan, differing only by the extra input U_ba and the inserted G_cA block, and in both
the summing junction prints a plus sign with no polarity on any input, so the feedback subtraction
the equations perform is invisible in the drawing.

Figures 7 to 10 are the paper's largest block and its least honest: four panels of five, five, six
and seven curves, each panel on a different y window, each identified only by inline end labels, and
Figure 9 prints seven labels for at most six curves with two of them floating in the middle of the
plot. Figure 7's own y title reads "Development Index(DJ)". Figures 11 and 12 re-read the Congo
forecast with and without the plan, once as six time series where the without-plan half is unreadable
and once as two trajectories in the index plane. Figure 13 is titled on its y axis only "Item" and
promises a perturbation the drawing never marks. Figure 14 is the sharpest caption defect on the
paper: it announces a two-dimensional concentration distribution under a Gaussian model and delivers
a one-dimensional cusp of about ten straight-interpolated points.

The tables carry the arithmetic and several of the faults. Table 1 builds a three-level indicator
tree in three columns, with "Pullotion" printed for pollution and the food-deficit indicator filed
under Education. Table 3 ranks ten countries and loses the country names of ranks 4 and 10 out of
their cells to the end of the text layer. Table 4 states the plan's effect in four sentences with no
numbers at all. Table 5 scores eighteen development activities, prints "Transferring the obtrusive
industries to the industrial towns" twice with two different scores, and files "The reduction of air
pollution" under social while its near-double sits under economic. Table 6 is the six-activity plan
with no scores, so it cannot be checked against Table 5 from its own page. Table 7 is the four-period
control scheme, where c1 reads 0.05 in all four periods and b3's entire row is printed with no
numbers.

Citation is uneven but not empty. Table 1 is the only exhibit the prose never names. Figures 1, 13
and 14 are each named a page before they print; Figures 5 and 6 are named only together, as
"Figures 5-6"; the p17 quartet is named twice as a rounded range ("Figures 7-10", then as the pairs
7-8 and 9-10); and Table 2, the one grid with no measured region, is cited twice while Table 1,
which is drawn and measured, is cited never.
rules: Measure first, then read the pixels: twenty-one measured regions resolve into fourteen figure rows, six table rows and one exclusion, with nothing unaccounted [place.area_frac].

A summary-sheet form is not an exhibit: the p1 region is the sheet's T1-T4 and F1-F4 fill-in rules plus its separator line, measured as one 0.77-area vector cluster because the rules span the page, so it is excluded rather than counted [place.area_frac].

Two measured regions under two printed captions are two rows with two verbatims, never one row with a union box: Figures 5 and 6 are pasted side by side on p13, and so are the two pairs on pp12, 17 and 18 [caption.verbatim].

When the text layer interleaves the captions of a two-column page into one run, the verbatim is typed from the crop and the source is marked accordingly; the eight captions on pp12, 13, 17 and 18 are the only such rows here [caption.numbering].
A caption hyphenated by the page is recorded as the layer prints it: Figure 2's verbatim keeps the 'Develop- ment' break instead of being repaired [caption.verbatim].

A numbered caption that the layer prints contiguously is quoted from the layer even when it carries a ligature, so Figure 13's and Figure 14's captions keep 'influences' as the f-ligature the page sets [caption.verbatim].

A shaded block matrix with two real index axes is heatmap-or-contour, not table-as-figure: Figure 2 draws nine filled blocks with a lattice inside each and ticks CI and DI along its edges [geometry.family].

A block diagram of boxes and arrows carrying a state vector is flowchart-or-schematic, and the three-aspect ring of Figure 1 takes the same family because its arcs are drawn as a cycle [geometry.family].

A state-space trajectory drawn as a joined path with markers is line, not scatter, even when each series has only two points: Figures 4 and 12 both draw the connector and both key their series with marker shapes [geometry.family].

A chart with no series key box is still legend 'inside' when the series are labelled at their own ends; all fourteen figure rows here label inline and not one carries an outside legend [geometry.legend].
A panel whose y axis is titled only 'Item' prints no quantity name, so printed_numbers records the ticks it does print and the note carries the missing title instead [geometry.printed_numbers].

Four panels of one figure family drawn on four different y windows are not a common scale: Figures 7 to 10 print 0.0260-0.0270, 0.022-0.032, 0.0260-0.0270 and 0.024-0.029 respectively, so shared_axes stays false [geometry.shared_axes].
Rows are counted as printed: Table 5 counts its three group-label rows as rows and Table 1 counts its seventeen indicator rows without the header [table.rows].
A group label set once and merged over its block makes merged_cells true, and the multi-line cell contents alone do not [table.merged_cells].

Count the physical columns, not the logical ones: Table 1 prints three level columns for a three-level tree, Table 3 prints eight columns of which seven are numeric, and Table 4 prints a two-by-two statement with a stub column [table.cols].
A table whose only rules are horizontal is booktabs even when it adds a rule at every group break, so all six grids here are booktabs and none is boxed [table.rule_style].
An exhibit first named a page before it prints takes a positive lead_pages: Figure 1 is named on p3 and printed on p4, Figures 13 and 14 are named a page early too [mention.lead_pages].
An exhibit the prose never names records count 0 with a null first_page and no style spelling - Table 1 here [mention.count].
A pointer hyphenated across a line break is quoted with the hyphen the layer keeps, so Figure 12's lead sentence begins 'Ac- cording to Figure 12' rather than being repaired [mention.lead_sentence].

tables.note: The indicator system, three columns headed Level1, Level2 and Level3, seventeen indicator rows. Environment covers the Population and Resources groups, Social covers Pullotion, Health, Education and Livelihood, Economic covers three indicators; the first two columns merge vertically over their groups, which is what makes seventeen rows read as a three-level tree. mention.lead_sentence: With the help of this research we can obtain Table 5 which reveals development activities and their score of effectiveness in

tables.note: Eighteen development activities, each scored to two decimals, sorted under three group labels - environmental, social, economic - that are set once per block and never repeated, so the group is carried by position and a rule rather than by a column of its own. Three printed columns: group, activity, score. Booktabs top and header rules, a rule at each group break, and no vertical strokes. Printed faults: 'Transferring the obtrusive industries to the industrial towns' appears twice, once at 0.13 and once at 0.19; 'The reduction of air pollution' is filed under social while its near-double sits under economic; the longest entry runs to the edge of the score column; and 'No damaging to the protected areas' closes the environmental block after the group rule has already been drawn.

caption.verbatim: Table 7: 20 years’ optimal control scheme for Congo

tables.caption_verbatim: Table 7: 20 years’ optimal control scheme for Congo

mention.lead_sentence: The revised control elements are shown in Table 7.

tables.note: The control scheme as a six-row plan: c1, c2, c3, b1, b2, b3 against four four-year periods headed 2014~2018, 2019~2023, 2024~2028 and 2029~2033, four numeric columns and one symbol column. Three-line ruling, nothing merged. Printed faults: c1's row is 0.05 in all four periods, which reads as a fill value rather than an optimised result; b3's row is printed with no numbers at all, its values pushed past the end of the text layer; the period headers use a tilde where the caption's own page prints an en dash elsewhere; the apostrophe in 'years'' is typographic while the rest of the paper's is not; and the decimal width swings from 0 to 0.05 to -0.1 within one row. No unit or scale is given for either control family.
